topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and introduces the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Immune Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of how the innate immune system detects danger through microbial patterns, cellular damage, and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the specific receptor families, downstream signaling cascades, and inflammasome complexes that translate danger detection into inflammatory mediator production.

topics.label: Cellular Activation and Leukocyte Recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how sentinel cells initiate local responses and guide circulating leukocytes through the vasculature into infected tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic Drainage and Adaptive Immune Priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how activated dendritic cells exit infected tissue through the lymphatic network to prime adaptive immune cells in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Pathophysiology of Systemic Inflammation and Sepsis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the severe physiological damage and high mortality that result when inflammatory cytokine production becomes systemic.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Inflammatory Resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the passive decay mechanisms and active biochemical switches that terminate acute inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Tissue Repair and Chronic Inflammatory Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the process of tissue reconstruction and the containment strategies that develop when inflammatory triggers cannot be cleared.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and provides a preview of the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
